case_name: Shri Bodhisattwa Gautam v Miss Subhra Chakraborty
respondent:
Miss Subhra Chakraborty
Supreme Court of India

15 December 1995
Special Leave Petition (Crl.) no. 2675 of 1995
The Judgment was delivered by: S. Saghir Ahmad, J.
1. Subhra Chakraborty (alias - Kalpana) who was a student of the Baptist College, Kohima where the opposite party, Shri Bodhisattwa Gautam was a lecturer, filed a complaint in the Court of the Judicial Magistrate, Ist Class, Kohima, Nagaland, alleging, inter alia, as under:

4. That, the accused person was in said Service in Kohima from April 1989 till he resigned the Service on 27th Jan, 1995 and was residing in a rented house in Kenezou Valley, Kohima owned by Dr. Zakiebatsu Angam.

facts: The complainant, Subhra Chakraborty (alias Kalpana), filed a complaint in the Court of the Judicial Magistrate, Ist Class, Kohima, Nagaland, alleging that she was in a love affair with Bodhisattwa Gautam, a lecturer at Baptist College, Kohima. She claimed that they had a secret marriage ceremony on September 20, 1993, and that Gautam had promised to marry her but instead abandoned her after she became pregnant twice.
Bodhisattwa Gautam was summoned in the criminal case registered as Criminal Case No. 1/95 under Sections 312/420/493/496/498-A of Indian Penal Code.

Gautam filed a petition in the Gauhati High Court u/s. 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing of the complaint and the proceedings initiated on its basis, but the High Court dismissed the petition.
Gautam then filed a Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No. 2675/95 with the Supreme Court, which was also dismissed.

The Supreme Court took suo motu notice to the facts of the case and issued notice to Gautam as to why he should not be asked to pay reasonable maintenance per month to the respondent during the pendency of the prosecution proceedings against him.
issues: Criminal offenses punishable under Indian Penal Code
petitioner_arguments: Gautam denied the allegations made against him in the complaint and stated that the complaint was filed only to harass and humiliate him.
He claimed that he had taken up service in another College, namely, Cachar College, but his services had since been terminated.
respondent_arguments: The complainant alleged that she was in a love affair with Gautam, who promised to marry her but instead abandoned her after she became pregnant twice.

She claimed that Gautam had committed criminal offenses punishable under Indian Penal Code and that he should be asked to pay reasonable maintenance per month during the pendency of the prosecution proceedings against him.
court_reasoning: The Supreme Court dismissed Gautam's Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No. 2675/95.

It took suo motu notice to the facts of the case and issued notice to Gautam as to why he should not be asked to pay reasonable maintenance per month to the respondent during the pendency of the prosecution proceedings against him.
holding: The Supreme Court dismissed Gautam's Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No. 2675/95.
It directed Gautam to pay reasonable maintenance per month to the respondent during the pendency of the prosecution proceedings against him.
